items.title: Pete Levin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: Peter Gabriel was also a tremendous artist and a very creative thinker. I always respected him for going out on live tours...

ctx.x: Almost more like an actress would. More like scripted. Want to stick to the script.

A little bit. Yeah that is it. If we could qualify it and make it a stage actress as opposed to film. Because things can change. I mean it’s never absolutely pat in the same way, otherwise why go to a concert, you’d better listen to the record. But to work out a show and know what’s going to happen, just work out the strongest way of putting the music across. That’s more important for a pop artist I think than a jazz artist. A jazz artist © Fillius Jazz Archive -19-

everybody knows is going to be different every time so it’s okay. I think somebody like Annie, where the fans really want to hear the song the way they just heard it on the record. Some of them would like it if it strays a little bit, a lot wouldn’t. Peter Gabriel was also a tremendous artist and a very creative thinker.
